title: Savings challenges are rigged against ADHD brains

beats.text: Unpopular opinion. Savings challenges are rigged against ADHD brains.
beats.why: Controversy hook: 'Unpopular opinion' + a strong claim invites comments and stitches (debate drives distribution; pattern widely used, ⚪ not measured by us). Names the exact category buyers already pay for (savings challenges: 1,049–2,376 review listings).

beats.text: Fifty two weeks, and zero reward until the very end. Of course you quit by week three.
beats.why: Backs the claim with the mechanism (delayed reward) + planner-fatigue relatability (@moveswithmaci 125.6k views).

beats.text: So we turned saving into a game.
Every time you save, you pop a bubble. Chain them, and you get combos.
beats.why: Real app screen recording. Watch-it-fill format: '100 envelope challenge' 2.8M views; 'color an icon' 202.5k.

beats.text: Hidden loot. Streaks that forgive a bad day. Levels that unlock new sprints.
beats.why: Gamification list: variable reward, forgiving streaks, progression.

beats.text: And when you finish one, it rains confetti. Tilt your phone, and it slides.
beats.why: Payoff moment: big celebration, tilt-reactive confetti (novel, demo-able).

beats.text: Twelve sprints, the app, and printable trackers. It's called Savings Sprints. Link in bio.
beats.why: What you get + exact product name.
